title: OPEN(STATUS=) — NEW errors on exist, OLD errors on missing, UNKNOWN is implementation-defined
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE OPEN_LOG(UNIT, FILE)
C     STATUS='UNKNOWN' is the F77 default. Behaviour is
C     implementation-defined: some compilers OPEN-or-CREATE, others
C     just fail. STATUS='NEW' fails when the file exists;
C     STATUS='OLD' fails when it doesn't; STATUS='REPLACE' truncates.
C     Java equivalent depends on FileOutputStream constructor flags
C     (append? truncate?).
      IMPLICIT NONE
      INTEGER UNIT
      CHARACTER*(*) FILE
      OPEN (UNIT=UNIT, FILE=FILE, STATUS='UNKNOWN')
      WRITE (UNIT, *) 'log opened'
      CLOSE (UNIT)
      END
notes: STATUS='UNKNOWN' is a frequent legacy default that papers over the open-or-create question. The rewrite MUST pick a deterministic semantic. The spec should flag this so the SME sign-off names append-vs-truncate explicitly.
